title: The Tryouts of Route 9
premise: Mara Eastwick has spent seventeen years keeping her head down in the fading mill town of Kettlebrook, hiding the strange gift she inherited from her grandmother: whatever feeling Mara kneads into dough, whoever eats it tastes that emotion. When she opens grandma's recipe box after the funeral, she finds cards written not for food but for a ritual — the Founding Bake, a tradition that has quietly held the town's memories together for two hundred years, and which is about to be erased by a developer's demolition order and a school board eager to forget. Pulled into the ritual alongside Theo Vance, the golden-boy class president whose perfect life is built on a family secret, Mara must gather six lost ingredients across town before prom night, when the last Bake can be performed. Each ingredient costs a memory — hers or someone else's — and by the end Mara must choose between restoring her own forgotten first love and saving the town that made her. She saves Kettlebrook, bakes her grief and love into one final loaf, and lets prom go on without her, whole but changed.
about_author: August Eriksen grew up above a bakery in rural Minnesota, where the smell of cardamom buns was indistinguishable from the smell of Sunday. A former line cook turned high-school English teacher, Eriksen writes stories about small towns that keep secrets in their kitchens.

chapters.title: Cardamom and Static
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At her grandmother's funeral reception, Mara bakes trays of comfort cookies that leave mourners weeping with relief, confirming the gift she's always hidden. She inherits the recipe box but doesn't open it yet. Emotional beat: grief wrapped in the discipline of staying invisible.

chapters.title: The Box That Isn't for Bread
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Alone in the bakery at 3 a.m., Mara opens the box and finds cards reading like spells — 'for remembering what the river took,' 'for untying a promise.' The last card is dated prom night, this year. Beat: dread and fascination colliding.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At school, Mara navigates the announcement that the Old Mill — site of the town's founding bake ovens — will be demolished the week after prom. Theo Vance gives the student-council speech supporting it, all smiles. Beat: the quiet fury of watching your history voted away.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Tastes Like Nothing
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo buys a roll from Mara's family stall and tastes absolutely nothing — no baked-in feeling, as if he's been hollowed out. He notices Mara noticing. Beat: two guarded people recognizing each other's armor.

chapters.title: First Card: River Water Boiled Twice
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Following the first recipe card, Mara wades into the Kettle River at dawn and pulls up a sealed jar; touching it floods her with a stranger's memory of the flood of 1927. Beat: awe curdling into fear — the ingredients remember.

chapters.title: Detention with the Dead
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo catches Mara sneaking back soaked and muddy; detention together forces an uneasy truce. He admits he felt nothing from her bread and asks why. She lies badly. Beat: reluctant alliance, first crack in both facades.

chapters.title: Second Card: Salt From a Broken Home
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The second ingredient requires salt kept in a house where a family fell apart — Theo's house. His parents' divorce left a cellar full of it. Mara witnesses the emptiness behind his perfection. Beat: intimacy through shared damage.

chapters.title: The Board Votes to Forget
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The school board fast-tracks the demolition; Mara speaks and is dismissed as 'the baker girl.' Grandma's old friend, Mrs. Okafor, slips Mara a note: 'The Bake holds us. Ask what happens when it stops.' Beat: isolation sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Third Card: Honey Owed to a Beekeeper
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. They track honey owed since 1954 to the last beekeeper on Route 9, who demands payment in memory: Theo surrenders his memory of winning state. He can't recall why the trophy matters anymore. Beat: the price becomes real and personal.

chapters.title: What the Town Tasted in 1927
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Researching in the library basement, Mara learns the Founding Bake fed the whole town once a generation, binding shared memory so Kettlebrook never repeated its worst mistakes. Skipping Bakes correlate with the town's decline. Beat: the stakes widen beyond prom.

chapters.title: Fourth Card: Flour Ground at Midnight
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They grind wheat in the abandoned mill itself, nearly caught by the developer's security — and find evidence the developer knows exactly what the mill is and wants it destroyed deliberately. Beat: the enemy has a face and a motive.

chapters.title: Prom Committee Sabotage
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo's council rival frames Mara for stealing prom funds, threatening expulsion days before the Bake. Theo burns his own reputation defending her, splitting from his family's expectations. Beat: love choosing sides against duty.

chapters.title: Fifth Card: Yeast From a Living Promise
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The fifth ingredient is starter culture kept alive by unbroken promise — Mrs. Okafor's, tended sixty years for a friend who never came home from the war. She passes it on, finally allowed to stop waiting. Beat: tenderness and release.

chapters.title: The Memory Mara Sold
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Reassembling clues, Theo realizes Mara already paid once: her earliest memory of her grandmother was traded years ago to keep the bakery alive — which is why she can't taste her own grief. Beat: devastating revelation, reversed sympathy.

chapters.title: Sixth Card: The Baker's Own Heart, Divided
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The final card demands the baker's heart 'divided' — half given willingly to another. Mara understands she must give Theo something true, and he must accept knowing it may be taken. Beat: confession under pressure; first kiss, freighted with cost.

chapters.title: Demolition Day Moves Up
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The developer, revealed as descended from the family whose founding betrayal the Bake preserves, moves demolition to prom night itself. The town's forgetting has been engineered for decades. Beat: clock compressed, villain unmasked.

chapters.title: Everything We Kneaded
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Prom begins; while the gym glitters, Mara and Theo smuggle six ingredients into the mill and begin the Bake as wrecking equipment idles outside. The oven, cold for thirty years, lights on its own. Beat: breathless momentum, wonder amid danger.

chapters.title: The Choice in the Dough
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mid-Bake, the ritual demands its final price: restore Mara's stolen memory or anchor the town's. Her hands move before her mind decides — she folds herself into the loaf. Beat: sacrifice as identity; the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: Bread for Two Hundred Years
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The Bake completes as dawn breaks; the mill stands, the demolition order dissolves into bureaucratic dust, and the whole town wakes tasting a memory they didn't know they'd lost. Mara doesn't wake with them. Beat: triumph shadowed by absence.

chapters.title: Prom Without Me
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara surfaces hours later, missing her grandmother's face entirely but carrying everyone else's memories like borrowed coats. Theo meets her at the gym doors with two corsages and tells her who she is, piece by piece. Beat: love as remembrance offered freely.

chapters.title: The New First Card
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Summer. Mara writes a new card in her own hand — 'for beginning again without forgetting' — and slides it atop grandma's stack. The bakery reopens; Mrs. Okafor tends the starter; Route 9 hums. Beat: inheritance accepted, tradition renewed.

chapters.title: What I Baked You
chapters.summary: Dual POV, converging. At the re-dedicated mill, Mara hands Theo a loaf baked with everything she now remembers of them — including the parts she chose to keep even when forgetting would hurt less. He takes a bite and remembers too. Final beat: survival's price paid, love chosen twice.
